title: noah-chen-sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-28.json
content:
SRE On-call scratchpad - Noah Chen - 2026-03-28

Summary:
- Night shift handover at 00:30 UTC. Briefed on elevated 5xx rate affecting hosted-api (region: us-west-2).
- Pager: INC-4532 triggered at 02:18 UTC for 5xx spikes on /v1/generate route.

Timeline / Notes:
- 02:18 UTC: Alert fired, initial investigation: error logs show downstream KV cache timeouts and some model-serving pods restarting.
- 02:22 UTC: Rotated traffic to fallback model group (model-v2-quant) using routing policy; immediate 20% drop in 5xx.
- 02:30 UTC: Identified one node with repeated OOMs in dedup-cache process (pod infer-cache-7f8d). Increased memory limit temporarily and cordoned node.
- 02:45 UTC: Restarted affected pod; cache warm-up increased latency briefly but errors reduced.
- 03:10 UTC: Pager stable, incident declared mitigated. Follow-up tasks assigned.

Actions taken (short):
- Applied temporary memory bump to infer-cache StatefulSet on us-west-2 cluster.
- Rerouted 15% traffic to fallback model group for safety window (policy TTL: 30m).
- Opened INC-4533 to track root cause and permanent fix.

Follow-ups / TODOs (for post-incident):
- [ ] Deep-dive with serving-runtime team on cache eviction/oom pattern (owner: Priya) - target by 2026-04-02.
- [ ] Add pod-level OOMGuard and proact alert for repeated restarts (owner: Noah) - propose runbook change.
- [ ] Update routing policy to automatically throttle traffic to fallback after N errors (product + runtime) - RFC.
- [ ] Perf test model-v2-quant with typical prefix patterns to ensure quality regressions are acceptable (eng-applied-ml).
- [ ] Document hotfix steps in CONFLUENCE:runbook-cache-eviction and link to incident playbook.

Runbook notes / ideas:
- Add explicit check for KV cache latency > 200ms to trigger preemptive eviction instead of letting OOMs happen.
- Consider limitrange changes for stateful cache pods; current mem requests might be too low for bursty workloads.
- When rerouting to fallback, we need a canary percentage ramping plan (5% -> 15% -> 50%)

Quick commands used:
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=infer-cache -o wide
- kubectl -n prod patch sts infer-cache --patch 'spec: template: spec: containers: - name: cache: resources: limits: memory: 6Gi'
- curl -sS "https://observability.internal/api/alerts?incident=INC-4532" | jq .

Notes to self / handoff for next shift:
- Check INC-4533 for RCA updates; ensure Priya has access to memory profiling artifacts.
- Validate that fallback model metrics (latency, tokens/success) are within SLO after 30m.
- If similar pattern repeats, escalate to infra (possible kernel-level memory leak).

Unresolved questions:
- Why did only one node show OOMs? Node selector + workload distribution check pending.
- Is cache warm-up causing unacceptable latency for high qps prefixes? Need telemetry.

Links:
- Incident: JIRA INC-4532, INC-4533
- Runbook: CONFLUENCE:runbook-cache-eviction
- PR for temporary memory bump: GITHUB:repo/infer-runtime/pull/412

Misc TODO (personal):
- Write short postmortem draft (1 pager) by EOD 2026-03-29.
- Schedule follow-up sync with serving-runtime and applied-ml (30m) next Tues.

End of scratchpad.
